title: U.S. Position at Upcoming G-7 Meeting
heading: Memorandum From Stephen P. Farrar to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Establishes the administration’s starting position on IMF quotas, international debt guarantees, and G-7 economic surveillance. Contrasts U.S. resistance to additional taxpayer exposure with French and Japanese proposals, and connects institutional reform to the impending debt-strategy review.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–001, Other (January - March 1989). No classification marking.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 5–7; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Three-page action memorandum, initialed by Farrar and stamped as seen by the National Security Adviser. The approval and disapproval lines on PDF page 7 are blank. No classification marking appears on the selected pages.
editorialReview: Use as an opening institutional-policy document. The recommendation to seek a Brady debriefing is a proposal, not evidence that the briefing occurred.
modelAssessment: Use as an opening statement of U.S. preferences on Fund resources, debt guarantees, and surveillance. It shows proposed resistance and alternatives before the strategy matured.
modelFollowUp: Find Treasury’s position and the instructions or decisions adopted after this recommendation.

title: Paris Economic Summit Preparatory Meeting
heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: Consider for the opening of the Paris summit sequence: records the agenda reaching Scowcroft after the February Sherpa meeting and the NSC assessment of French intentions. Connects monetary coordination, debt, East-West trade, and the environment before the principals set U.S. objectives.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Subject Files, OA/ID CF00972–002, Paris Economic Summit [July 1989]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 24; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The one-page memorandum is at PDF page 24, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” The attached six-page Sherpa report is represented by a withdrawal sheet on page 25; its contents are not reconstructed here.
editorialReview: Compare with any released copy of McCormack’s report. If that fuller account is selected, consider citing this covering assessment in annotation.
modelAssessment: Retain the NSC assessment if it adds policy judgment beyond the underlying Sherpa report; otherwise use it to annotate that fuller record.
modelFollowUp: Compare McCormack’s report with the U.S. instructions and the subsequent summit discussion.

title: White House Summit Group Meeting on Paris Summit
heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: Use in annotation to the March 20 Scowcroft memorandum: the marked action copy shows the staff recommendation and an approval check for arranging the White House Summit Group meeting.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Subject Files, OA/ID CF00972–002, Paris Economic Summit [July 1989]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 8; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Use the annotated copy on page 8; page 10 is a parallel copy with a blank approval line. Page 8 bears a “SIGNED” stamp, an approval check, and a handwritten organizational instruction. It has added Confidential stamps alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings. The selected copy’s terminal Confidential stamp controls this Source Note.
editorialReview: Do not attribute the handwritten instruction to a particular person without checking the handwriting. Describe the marked copy without printing both copies as separate documents.
modelAssessment: Use the action copy to explain preparation and routing of the March 20 paper. Meeting organization alone is insufficient for a separate policy document.
modelFollowUp: Locate the substantive discussion or conclusions of the proposed White House Summit Group meeting.

title: Paris Economic Summit
heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to the White House Chief of Staff (Sununu)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: Consider for documenting who set summit strategy: Scowcroft asks his co-chair Sununu to bring Baker and Brady into a White House Summit Group discussion before securing the President’s guidance for the next Sherpa meeting.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Subject Files, OA/ID CF00972–002, Paris Economic Summit [July 1989]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 3; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed copy is on page 3. The undated copy on page 11 is not a second proposal. The selected copy has added Confidential stamps at top and bottom alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings; the Source Note reflects the terminal stamp. The Sherpa report remains withdrawn (page 4); agenda, participants, and organization chart follow on pages 5–7.
editorialReview: Retain the dated copy as this proposal’s citation copy; compare the organizational annotation on Melby’s March 15 action memorandum. Initials do not by themselves establish subsequent implementation.
modelAssessment: Select if the allocation of authority materially explains how summit objectives were settled; pair it with the substantive objectives.
modelFollowUp: Find the principals’ discussion and the President’s guidance for the next Sherpa meeting.

title: Economic Policy Directive 1
heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: Propose for the institutional origins of Bush trade policy. Melby recommends preserving NSC review of the EPC trade strategy because trade with Japan, Europe, and developing countries has national-security implications; he invokes the handling of debt as a precedent.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Subject Files, OA/ID CF00972–018, Trade. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 10; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Page 10 is the dated, initialed Melby memorandum, routed through Deal; its approval lines are blank. Page 11 is an undated memorandum prepared for Scowcroft to send to Brady, with a typed name and no visible signature. Brady’s March 21 directive is on pages 12–13. None of these pages should be assigned the date of another document.
editorialReview: Use the Melby action memorandum for the recommendation actually evidenced here. Check whether Scowcroft’s proposed reply was signed or sent before describing it as an executed instruction.
modelAssessment: The selection value lies in the proposed NSC role in trade strategy and the reason for it. Establish the recommendation before describing any resulting directive.
modelFollowUp: Find the signed or sent reply and the economic-policy directive or review record to which it responded.

title: Proposed U.S. Contribution to the IMF’s Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility
heading: Draft Report of the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies to President Bush and Congress
dateBasis: April 1989 on the title page. April 7, the Treasury circulation date, is used only as a sorting key; no day is printed on the report.
sender: National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies
selectionRationale: Explains the case for a $150 million U.S. contribution to the IMF’s concessional lending facility for poorer countries. Connects U.S. influence, reform conditions, arrears, interest subsidies, and collaboration with the World Bank and IDA, with tables on contributors and costs.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–004, Chron File: April 1989 [1]. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 16 released report pages; PDF pages 13–28; includes title page and five tables
evidenceNotes: Treasury draft circulated for interagency clearance. Title page dated April 1989; ten numbered text pages and five tables follow, ending on PDF page 28. April 7 transmission papers and an April 10 NSC concurrence surround the report. No classification marking appears on the selected report pages.
editorialReview: Compare with the final transmitted or published NAC report before choosing the controlling text. The proposal documents the administration’s case for contributing, not enactment or payment of the appropriation.
modelAssessment: The draft makes the policy and funding case for ESAF. Prefer the decisive internal recommendation or final transmitted report if available, using this draft to document any significant change.
modelFollowUp: Locate the final report and the decision on the U.S. contribution; compare the draft before treating its language as an adopted position.

title: Briefing for the President’s Lunch with World Bank President Conable
heading: Memorandum From Roger B. Porter to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Brings together the World Bank and IMF role in financing Brady-plan debt reduction, the ninth replenishment of IDA, and the political versus technical basis for China lending. Quantifies the gap between Conable’s preferred IDA funding level and likely U.S. congressional support.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–009, Chron File: June 1989 [1]. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 12–13; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page presidential briefing dated June 20 for the June 21 luncheon, initialed by Porter. Separate talking-point cards follow on PDF pages 14–15. No classification marking appears on the two briefing pages.
editorialReview: Use the June 20 preparation date rather than the June 21 meeting date. Pair with Deal’s June 21 corrections, especially on the number of China loans and the state of IDA negotiations.
modelAssessment: Select if this is the clearest record of the World Bank resource and debt-financing choices put before Bush; read it with Deal’s corrections.
modelFollowUp: Seek the June 21 lunch record and subsequent IDA and debt-financing instructions.

title: Conable Meeting: NSC Corrections on Debt, IDA, and China Lending
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Shows the NSC refining the President’s institutional briefing: distinguishing positions among creditor banks, postponing premature IDA negotiations, and correcting the China loan pipeline. It also explains the relationship between IMF membership and entry into the World Bank.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–009, Chron File: June 1989 [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 19–20; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum routed through Deane Hoffmann, initialed by Deal and stamped “APNSA Has Seen.” The selected copy on PDF pages 19–20 repeats the memorandum on pages 10–11; it is counted once.
editorialReview: Retain the corrections as a distinct document, rather than silently rewriting Porter’s briefing. Treat the membership discussion as institutional eligibility policy; bilateral Soviet relations are not the reason for selection.
modelAssessment: Retain the points that alter the President’s understanding of the institutional choices. Consider annotating Porter’s briefing if the corrections can be conveyed concisely.
modelFollowUp: Compare the lunch record, corrected loan information, and the positions actually conveyed to Conable.

title: Presidential Briefing on Economic Summit, 2:15 p.m., Monday, June 26, 1989, Cabinet Room
heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: Use in annotation to identify the staff preparation and routing of Scowcroft’s June 24 presidential briefing. Establishes the planned division of roles between Scowcroft and Sununu.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Latin American Files, Economic Chronological Files, OA/ID 91139–001, Latin America - Economics (June 1989). No classification marking.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 9; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The one-page action memorandum is routed through Deane E. Hoffmann and asks Scowcroft to sign the attached presidential memorandum. It supplies June 21 as the staff-paper date; June 26 is the scheduled meeting date. The attached presidential memorandum appears separately on pages 3–5.
editorialReview: Do not date the presidential briefing June 21 or June 26. Compare handwritten concurrences before attributing drafting or clearance beyond the typed routing.
modelAssessment: Annotate the preparation of the June 24 briefing; avoid giving staff routing the same weight as presidential objectives.
modelFollowUp: Find a record of the June 26 briefing and subsequent Paris bargaining.

title: Baker to Scowcroft: Coordination of U.S. Votes on IFI Loan Requests
heading: Memorandum From James A. Baker III to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: A principal-level request for Scowcroft to redesign consultation before U.S. votes in the financial institutions. Baker accepts economic tests for most loans but argues that Treasury’s short-notice instructions can exclude important foreign-policy considerations.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–014, Chron File: July 1989 [3]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 64; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Signed one-page memorandum dated June 22 with a State declassification notation. A duplicate is filed on PDF page 78; the attached State analysis and executive-order extracts are separate documents.
editorialReview: Select as the initiating principal-level intervention and pair with Scowcroft’s July 25 response. Distinguish Baker’s account of the Philippines vote from an independently checked World Bank voting record.
modelAssessment: A strong opening to the loan-vote sequence: a principal identifies the conflict between financial review and foreign-policy consultation.
modelFollowUp: Follow through the alternatives and July 25 instruction, then compare how the appeals process operated.

title: Meeting with the White House Summit Group
heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. A compact statement of U.S. objectives for the Paris summit: stronger monetary coordination, support for the Brady debt strategy, resistance to competing debt proposals, and an ambitious Uruguay Round. It connects exchange-rate policy, commercial-bank negotiations, and presidential bargaining.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Latin American Files, Economic Chronological Files, OA/ID 91139–001, Latin America - Economics (June 1989). Secret.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 3–5; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The initialed three-page briefing is dated June 24; June 26 is the meeting it prepares. Its location in Latin American Files does not limit its substantive coverage to that region. The opening withdrawal inventory lists it, but the three released pages and declassification stamp are present. Page 12 still represents a withheld one-page biography. Agendas and talking points are separate attachments.
editorialReview: Propose the three-page briefing as one document. Route Mexico-specific material by substance while retaining the multilateral debt strategy in Volume XXX; do not mistake the old withdrawal inventory for the present release state.
modelAssessment: A strong statement of U.S. objectives across monetary coordination, debt, and trade. Preserve the relationships among those choices.
modelFollowUp: Compare with Treasury and State instructions, presidential guidance, and the summit conversation record.

title: Improving the Interagency Loan Review Process
heading: Memorandum From William Milam to Eugene J. McAllister
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Supplies concrete alternatives behind the Baker–Scowcroft intervention: minimum notice before negative votes, NSC arbitration, or voting among the principal reviewing agencies. Uses Haiti and Egypt loans to show that the consultation problem extended beyond the Philippines.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–014, Chron File: July 1989 [3]. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 69–70; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page State memorandum stamped June 29, 1989. The first page identifies Milam and McAllister; the final-page drafting line gives June 28. No classification marking appears on the memorandum pages.
editorialReview: Use the June 29 memorandum date and preserve the separate drafting date. These are staff proposals, not adopted procedures; compare with Scowcroft’s later signed instruction.
modelAssessment: Useful for the actual procedural alternatives considered. If the July 12 assessment adequately preserves them, this paper may serve in annotation.
modelFollowUp: Compare the options with Scowcroft’s July 25 instruction and any agreed operating procedure.

title: Development-Bank Votes: Deal’s Recommendation to Scowcroft
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Explains where the loan-review machinery failed: Treasury could depart from staff consensus without enough time for State to appeal. Recommends formal notice and an appeal route, anticipates Treasury’s objections, and places the dispute within the National Advisory Council’s responsibilities.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–014, Chron File: July 1989 [3]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 60–61; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page action memorandum, initialed by Deal, with Paal and Rostow concurrences and a handwritten concurrence notation. The memorandum is duplicated on PDF pages 82–83 and counted once. An undated version of the proposed Scowcroft response follows on pages 62–63.
editorialReview: Pair with Baker’s request and Scowcroft’s dated, signed July 25 memorandum. Do not use the undated attachment as a second document selection.
modelAssessment: A strong analytical companion to the signed instruction because it explains the failure in consultation and the proposed remedy.
modelFollowUp: Compare the final instruction and Treasury’s response, including any change to the proposed appeal route.

title: International Debt: Commercial Banks and Official Financing
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Explains strains in the Brady strategy across several borrowers and the division of responsibility between commercial creditors and the IMF and World Bank. The Philippines discussion is especially revealing: banks proposed new money while expecting the institutions to finance debt reduction.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Latin American Files, Economic Chronological Files, OA/ID 91139–002, Latin America - Economics (July - October 1989). Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 14–15; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated July 21, initialed by Deal and stamped as seen. The selected copy carries a handwritten “Good memo” comment. The Negroponte cable is an attachment outside the two-page extent.
editorialReview: Attribute market assessments and predictions to Deal and his unnamed banking contacts. Use the comparative discussion to explain official/private burden sharing, not as proof that predicted moratoria occurred.
modelAssessment: Select for the allocation of debt-reduction costs between commercial creditors and multilateral institutions. Country cases should illustrate that general strategy.
modelFollowUp: Compare Treasury’s Brady-strategy instructions with the relevant institutional financing decisions.

title: Scowcroft’s Instruction to Review Development-Bank Voting Procedures
heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Acting Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
recipient: The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Acting Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency
selectionRationale: A signed Scowcroft instruction calling for advance notice and an appeals process when U.S. development-bank votes carry foreign-policy consequences. Assigns a review to the international-economics PCC, with unresolved options to go to the President through the Treasury Secretary.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00695–014, Chron File: July 1989 [3]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 76–77; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated July 25, with Scowcroft’s signature on the second page and staff annotations. It specifies an August 25 target for the review. The undated copy on PDF pages 62–63 is not counted separately.
editorialReview: Distinguish the instruction to develop procedures from evidence that the review was completed. Link to the June 1991 Philippines dispute, where Deal explicitly invokes the resulting appeals mechanism.
modelAssessment: An anchor for the sequence: it directs advance notice and review of an appeals mechanism. Do not equate the instruction to review arrangements with proof that all resulting procedures were settled.
modelFollowUp: Find the PCC review and resulting procedure, then connect it to the June 1991 Philippine-loan appeal.

title: Scowcroft to Bush: Negotiating an Increase in IMF Quotas
heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Reveals the difference between the public U.S. bargaining position on IMF quotas and the increase Bush had authorized negotiators to accept. Places the U.S. position against demands from other Fund members and links the decision to correspondence with Chancellor Kohl.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00696–001, Chron File: December 1989 [1]. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 39; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: One-page action memorandum dated December 28, 1989, initialed by Scowcroft and stamped “The President Has Seen” and “Signed.” No classification marking appears on this selected memorandum; the signed outgoing January 2 letter follows on PDF page 42.
editorialReview: Keep the December memorandum distinct from the January 2 presidential letter. Compare the final letter and Treasury drafts when annotating the public presentation of the quota decision.
modelAssessment: Select for the distinction between the public bargaining position and the negotiating authority reported in the paper.
modelFollowUp: Compare the outgoing correspondence, Treasury instructions, international agreement, and later U.S. authorization.

title: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development: French Initiative
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Explains how France and the EC shaped the new bank before U.S. negotiating positions were settled. Identifies the stakes in membership, democratic conditionality, creditor control, capital shares, and the precedent for admission to other financial institutions.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 6–7; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page information memorandum, initialed by Deal, with a seen stamp and declassification notation. Records the January 6 telephone conversation and Key West Sherpa discussions as antecedents.
editorialReview: Select for the origins of U.S. institutional bargaining over the EBRD. Attribute judgments about Attali and European motives to Deal.
modelAssessment: Useful for the early institutional choices. Compare with the January 9 briefing and January 16 report before deciding how much preliminary explanation requires full text.
modelFollowUp: Identify which membership, capital, and lending conditions entered the U.S. negotiating instructions.

title: Baker–Brady–Scowcroft Conclusions: China Lending and the EBRD
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Records agreed U.S. instructions on delaying and limiting World Bank loans to China, seeking G-7 coordination, and entering EBRD negotiations with specified conditions. Provides decision evidence across two financial institutions.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 9–10; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum headed “Summary of Conclusions of Meeting with Secretaries Baker and Brady on January 9: China and EBRD.” Initialed by Deal and stamped as seen; the profile on PDF page 8 records “Noted by Scowcroft.”
editorialReview: Treat as Deal’s contemporary summary of conclusions, not a verbatim meeting transcript. Link the basic-human-needs lending policy to the already proposed July 1990 China-lending papers.
modelAssessment: A strong link between proposed policy and agreed instructions. Preserve the distinction between Deal’s report of conclusions and any separately approved meeting record.
modelFollowUp: Seek the underlying conclusions or implementing instructions on World Bank China loans and EBRD participation.

title: EBRD: Brief for the Baker–Brady–Scowcroft Meeting
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal, Adrian Basora, and Condoleezza Rice to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
sender: Timothy E. Deal, Adrian Basora, and Condoleezza Rice
selectionRationale: Sets out NSC recommendations on borrower eligibility, the private-sector mandate, and membership for the EC Commission and European Investment Bank. Shows the proposed diplomatic campaign to change the bank’s design before negotiations.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 11–12; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page joint memorandum, routed through Blackwill and Deal, with initials and a seen stamp. The printed sender line spells Rice’s first name “Condoleeza”; the heading uses her standard name. The Mulford attachment begins on PDF page 13 and is outside this item’s extent.
editorialReview: Pair with the separate January 9 conclusions to distinguish proposed positions from the principals’ resulting instructions.
modelAssessment: Retain the proposed eligibility and mandate rules if they establish the position taken into negotiations; use overlapping background in annotation.
modelFollowUp: Compare the principals’ conclusions and the delegation’s instructions with the January 16 negotiating report.

title: EBRD Negotiations: Joint Treasury–State–NSC Assessment
heading: Memorandum From David C. Mulford, Richard T. McCormack, and Timothy E. Deal to Nicholas F. Brady, James A. Baker III, and Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
sender: David C. Mulford, Richard T. McCormack, and Timothy E. Deal
recipient: Nicholas F. Brady, James A. Baker III, and Brent Scowcroft
selectionRationale: Gives the negotiating team’s common account of U.S. isolation over the new bank’s size, lending mandate, eligibility, capital denomination, and governance. Particularly useful for the concern that infrastructure lending could displace support for private enterprise.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 30–32; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Three-page Treasury memorandum dated January 16, naming all three officials as senders and all three principals as recipients. Filed as the attachment to Deal’s January 22 report. The final page promises a later paper with recommended positions.
editorialReview: Preserve joint authorship and the January 16 document date rather than the January 22 cover date. Pair with Deal’s separate personal assessment, which explicitly supplements this joint memorandum.
modelAssessment: A strong candidate because the negotiating team reports concrete obstacles and disagreements over institutional design.
modelFollowUp: Compare with the agreed U.S. instructions and the later terms recommended to the President.

title: Negotiations for the EBRD: Deal’s Assessment
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Shows the practical limits on U.S. influence in a European-led financial institution. Weighs participation on unwelcome terms against staying out, and assesses differences among prospective borrowers over markets, privatization, and infrastructure finance.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 27–29; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Three-page information memorandum with initials and a seen stamp. Its attachment is the separately proposed January 16 joint memorandum on PDF pages 30–32.
editorialReview: Retain as a distinct assessment rather than a duplicate of the attached negotiating report. Attribute its candid descriptions and judgments to Deal.
modelAssessment: Retain if Deal’s assessment explains a consequential choice between participation and withdrawal that is not adequately captured in the joint report.
modelFollowUp: Find the principals’ response; compare the January 16 report to avoid repeating its negotiation narrative.

title: IEPR Breakfast: EBRD Conditions, Egypt and the IMF, China Loans
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal and Eric Melby to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
sender: Timothy E. Deal and Eric Melby
selectionRationale: Connects U.S. negotiating instructions on the EBRD charter with pressure for IMF flexibility toward Egypt and scheduling of World Bank loans to China. Shows how the same principals managed political conditions and financial discipline across institutions.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Secret.
extentLabel: 3 partly released memorandum pages; PDF pages 35–37; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Three-page memorandum dated January 25 for the January 26 breakfast. Marked “Declassified in Part”; substantial blocks on PDF pages 36 and 37 remain redacted. The visible text supports the institutional proposals summarized here.
editorialReview: Propose the released institutional-policy passages, preserving the redaction notices. Do not reconstruct the withheld text or describe the memorandum as fully released.
modelAssessment: Propose an institutional-policy extract if the released passages add distinctive choices on the EBRD, IMF, or World Bank. Preserve redactions and identify omitted unrelated material.
modelFollowUp: Find conclusions of the breakfast and fuller released copies of the relevant institutional papers.

title: EBRD: Conditions for U.S. Participation
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Identifies the conditions that could keep the United States out of the EBRD. Explains why paying capital in a floating ECU raised concerns about open-ended U.S. commitments and precedents for the IMF, World Bank, and regional development banks.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–008, Other (January - May 1990) [1]. Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 47–48; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page action memorandum. A handwritten mark appears on the approval line on PDF page 48. The attached presidential memorandum on PDF pages 49–52 is a draft revised by State; it is not treated as a signed presidential decision.
editorialReview: Distinguish approval to convey Scowcroft’s concurrence from final presidential approval of U.S. membership. Note that the text expressly withholds attribution to Scowcroft of the Secretaries’ ECU position.
modelAssessment: The currency-denomination and financial-exposure problem gives this paper broader significance than a routine progress report.
modelFollowUp: Trace the approval to inform Mulford into the instructions sent and the final capital arrangements.

title: U.S. Membership in the EBRD: Brief for the President’s Brady Meeting
heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Presents Scowcroft’s recommendation to join the EBRD despite incomplete success in negotiations. Specifies public/private lending proportions, voting thresholds, borrower categories, and a mechanism to suspend lending after retreat from political or economic reform.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–010, Other (March 1990). Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 4–5; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page briefing memorandum headed “Meeting with Secretary of the Treasury Nicholas Brady,” dated March 8, with the President-has-seen stamp. The meeting is listed for 1:30–1:50 p.m. in the Oval Office; this is the preparatory brief, not minutes.
editorialReview: Use the recommendation and negotiated package as evidence of U.S. institutional policy. Verify the President’s actual instructions against a separate decision or meeting record; the seen stamp alone does not establish them.
modelAssessment: A strong decision-stage paper: Scowcroft recommends joining and specifies governance and lending terms. It remains a briefing, not minutes of the meeting.
modelFollowUp: Find the President’s disposition and compare the charter and U.S. participation authority with the recommended terms.

title: EBRD: Lending Rules, Capital, and Governance Negotiations
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
selectionRationale: Reports agreement on the 40/60 public/private lending split and acceptance of European Investment Bank membership, while capital denomination, U.S. shares, board arrangements, and leadership remained unsettled. Offers a concrete record of how institutional design was negotiated.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–010, Other (March 1990). Confidential.
extentLabel: 2 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 10–11; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Two-page information memorandum, initialed by Deal, with Robert Blackwill’s concurrence on the final page. The printed memorandum is addressed to Scowcroft; the seen stamp identifies the Deputy National Security Adviser.
editorialReview: Focus selection on the lending mandate, capital and governance provisions. The discussion of Soviet borrowing is relevant here as a question of bank eligibility and voting rules.
modelAssessment: Use the changed lending and membership terms to document movement toward agreement. Consider annotation if a later report captures these changes and their causes more fully.
modelFollowUp: Locate resolution of the remaining capital, shareholding, board, and leadership questions.

title: IEPR Breakfast: Arrears, IMF Programs, and Development-Bank Lending
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
institutions: IMF; World Bank; Inter-American Development Bank; EBRD
selectionRationale: Shows U.S. choices over clearing Honduran arrears to the IMF, World Bank and IDB; pressing for an IMF mission to Egypt; and conditioning Zambian debt relief on an IMF or World Bank program. Also records remaining EBRD governance questions.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91148–010, Other (March 1990). Confidential.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 13–15; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: Three-page memorandum dated March 28 for the March 29 breakfast, with a seen stamp and staff concurrences. The institutional and country-financing recommendations are visible on PDF pages 13–15.
editorialReview: Prioritize the EBRD and country-financing portions for document treatment. The intervening bilateral U.S.–Soviet trade discussion can be omitted with an editorial indication and routed to the appropriate volume.
modelAssessment: Select the institutional passages on arrears, conditionality, and EBRD governance; their value is the relationship between financial rules and diplomatic priorities.
modelFollowUp: Find the principals’ conclusions and subsequent IMF, World Bank, or IDB action; mark any omitted bilateral material.

title: The Economic Summit at Houston
heading: Memorandum From Secretary of State Baker and Secretary of the Treasury Brady to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
sender: James A. Baker III and Nicholas F. Brady
selectionRationale: Propose alongside Scowcroft’s July 2 assessment. The joint State–Treasury paper sets negotiating objectives and anticipated G-7 positions on agriculture, Soviet and East European assistance, debt, the environment, and China lending. It provides the substantive baseline to which Scowcroft explicitly responds.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91149–006, Other (July 1990). Secret.
extentLabel: 8 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 16–23; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The eight-page document names both Baker and Brady on page 16. The withdrawal inventory describes Baker alone; the document heading supplies the fuller authorship. The release stamp and all eight document pages are present, ending with Secret on page 23. It is attached to the Houston briefing sequence in the Scowcroft chronological file.
editorialReview: Compare this citation copy with State and Treasury copies before final publication. The fact that it is in Scowcroft’s file does not make him an author or addressee. Coordinate regional passages with the relevant volumes.
modelAssessment: Use the joint State–Treasury assessment to establish the agencies’ proposed bargain, then compare Scowcroft’s response.
modelFollowUp: Find summit exchanges and subsequent instructions that establish which proposed positions became U.S. policy.

title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
heading: Memorandum From Meg Lundsager of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

evidenceNotes: One-page action memorandum dated July 1, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” It asks for Scowcroft’s signature on the attached memorandum. Neither this request nor the seen stamp establishes presidential approval.
editorialReview: The cover memorandum establishes association with the July 2 briefing, not an exact date or dispatch for its undated attachment. Leave difficult marginalia unattributed.
modelAssessment: Use for the association and timing of the undated China-lending attachment. The cover cannot supply a signed presidential decision.
modelFollowUp: Seek a controlling signed or annotated copy and the resulting U.S. voting instructions.

title: Scope Paper for Houston Summit
heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)

modelFollowUp: Compare the President’s briefing-book copy and the actual Houston discussions.

title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to President Bush
dateBasis: Undated document; sorted with the July 1, 1990 covering memorandum. Prepared for a July 2 briefing; that is not an established document date.
selectionRationale: High-priority proposal for the decision process on China lending. Weighs the weakening G-7 consensus, congressional restrictions, and World Bank plans, then recommends a compromise linking expanded lending to economic reform while preserving U.S. legal constraints.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91149–006, Other (July 1990). Confidential.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 6–8; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The three-page memorandum is undated and has a typed FROM line. Lundsager’s July 1 covering memorandum (page 5) prepared it for the July 2 briefing. The approval and disapproval lines on page 8 are blank. Page 7 prints “$700 billion,” while the conclusion on page 8 and talking points on page 9 say “$700 million”; preserve and flag this discrepancy in any transcription. The document is released despite its listing on the earlier withdrawal inventory.
editorialReview: Retain an undated dateline and do not claim approval or dispatch. Check the China-volume boundary and any signed or annotated parallel copy before final selection. July 1 is solely the chronology sorting reference supplied by the covering memorandum.
modelAssessment: Select for the interaction of World Bank lending policy, G-7 coordination, and U.S. legal constraints. The blank decision lines remain unresolved.
modelFollowUp: Locate the presidential disposition and U.S. board instructions; coordinate any China-specific narrative with the regional volume.

title: Houston Economic Summit
heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.
selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. Scowcroft links economic leadership to the NATO summit, recommends conditionality for Soviet assistance without a major U.S. cash commitment, and treats agricultural reform in the Uruguay Round as Houston’s central economic opportunity. His discussion connects German unification and COCOM reform with summit bargaining.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Chronological Files, OA/ID 91149–006, Other (July 1990). Confidential.
extentLabel: 3 released memorandum pages; PDF pages 12–14; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed memorandum occupies pages 12–14. Its first page refers to the Baker–Brady paper, and the July 1 Melby cover on page 15 identifies the two-paper package. All three pages are released and the terminal marking is Confidential. These recommendations do not by themselves establish the President’s decisions or summit outcomes.
editorialReview: Print as a distinct NSC assessment if space permits, with the Baker–Brady paper as a substantive companion. Compare the President’s briefing-book copy and subsequent summit conversations for annotations and outcome evidence.
modelAssessment: Select the distinct NSC judgment on the multilateral economic bargain, especially agriculture and assistance conditions; assess regional passages for cross-volume treatment.
modelFollowUp: Compare Baker–Brady’s recommendations with summit discussions and the agreed economic text.

title: Multilateral Assistance to Central America: Designing the Donor Mechanism
heading: Memorandum From David A. Pacelli and Meg Lundsager to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
sender: David A. Pacelli and Meg Lundsager
selectionRationale: Documents the unresolved design of a proposed G-24 donor mechanism and Treasury’s resistance to an inadequately specified fund. Shows the NSC insisting that State explain how the mechanism would fit the Enterprise for the Americas initiative and existing regional policy.

editorialReview: Keep the proposed Central American donor group distinct from the G-24 developing-country caucus at the IMF and World Bank. Pair with the October papers on competing funding mechanisms.
modelAssessment: Useful if it explains why a new donor mechanism was disputed and how it would relate to existing institutions. Compare later, fuller assessments for annotation alternatives.
modelFollowUp: Find State’s proposed design, Treasury’s response, and a decision on the donor mechanism.

title: OAS Debt Conversion Fund: U.S. Reservations
heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
institutions: Inter-American Development Bank; OAS; Development-finance coordination

modelAssessment: The choice between a new fund and existing IDB/AID programs is the institutional question to retain, together with its resource implications.
modelFollowUp: Locate the President’s response and the ensuing U.S. position on the proposed fund.

title: Enterprise for the Americas: Competing Funds and Coordination Problems
heading: Memorandum From Donald C. Johnson to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

editorialReview: Select chiefly for fund design, donor coordination, and the proposed resolution of overlapping mechanisms. Attribute its favorable assessment of EAI and criticisms of State to Johnson.
modelAssessment: Retain the competing institutional designs and donor-funding consequences. This supplies substantive disagreement behind the coordination papers.
modelFollowUp: Seek Treasury and State originals and the agreed division of responsibilities between their initiatives.

title: Funding the Partnership for Democracy and Development
heading: Memorandum From Donald C. Johnson and Eric D. Melby to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
sender: Donald C. Johnson and Eric D. Melby
selectionRationale: Shows how the NSC sought to rank competing multilateral funding appeals and reconcile State’s Central American partnership with the President’s EAI. Makes donor commitments, OMB clearance, and U.S. budget constraints central to the design of the new mechanism.

modelAssessment: Select for the allocation of scarce U.S. and donor resources if it explains a consequential funding choice; distinguish the marked action from later commitments.
modelFollowUp: Trace the approved staff action into OMB clearance, donor commitments, and the final funding arrangement.

title: World Bank and IDB Lending to Brazil: South America Follow-Up

title: Invoking the Appeals Process for a World Bank Loan to the Philippines
heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Wilma G. Hall and Dona F. Proctor (for delivery to Scowcroft)
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
recipient: Wilma G. Hall and Dona F. Proctor (for delivery to Scowcroft)
selectionRationale: Shows the 1989 consultation reform being invoked in practice when State and Treasury could not agree on a World Bank environmental loan. Explains why Scowcroft was asked to arbitrate and records the parties’ agreement to that procedure.

title: Baker’s Case for a Yes Vote on the Philippine World Bank Loan

evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated June 24, signed by Baker. The second page concludes by asking the President to direct a yes vote. No classification marking appears on the selected pages.

modelAssessment: Retain the principal-level alternative so the reader can assess the choice placed before the President, including the comparisons with other lenders.

title: Scowcroft’s Recommendation on the Philippine Environmental Loan
heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush

editorialReview: Keep the document undated, using the June 24 cover only for sorting. Compare the handwritten note and the President’s decision record before attributing final approval. Pair with Baker’s signed memorandum arguing for a yes vote.

title: IMF Quotas: U.S. Share and Congressional Approval

editorialReview: Attribute the numerical and budget-accounting explanation to Deal. Preserve the manuscript comments for editorial comparison, and check implementing legislation before describing the increase as effective.

title: Brady to Scowcroft: Funding International Priorities and the EAI
heading: Memorandum From Nicholas F. Brady to Brent Scowcroft
dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.
institutions: Multilateral Investment Fund; IMF; Development-finance coordination
selectionRationale: Shows how domestic appropriations constrained multilateral commitments. Brady warns that failure to fund the U.S. share of the EAI Multilateral Investment Fund could prevent other countries’ pledged contributions, and asks Scowcroft to review international-affairs priorities.
sourceNote: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Timothy E. Deal Files, Chronological Files, OA/ID CF00959–010, Chron File: March 1992 [1]. No classification marking.
extentLabel: 1 released memorandum page; PDF page 17; attachments described separately
evidenceNotes: One-page memorandum dated March 17, initialed by Brady. It refers to a prior presidential meeting on EAI and IMF priorities and to the March 31 expiration of the continuing resolution. No classification marking appears on the page.
editorialReview: Use for the relationship between U.S. budget choices and donor commitments. The memorandum reports pledges and funding risks, not completed contributions.
